title: Example 287 preservation at the frozen bound 80 again, on a checker whose ties take only code that cannot call back through the JDK
description: The preservation stream's step 5 (llm-dlc/loops/domain-advances-preservation.md), after job 20261117-180758-example-287-preservation-at-the-frozen-b. That job ran 424 s and 1187 paths, then stopped: no invariant for the previous release's BCrypt.key loop at pc 39, 'an iteration changes local 1, which holds a reference' (local 1 is the key array). Capped probes reach about 540 paths in 280 s, so they cannot get there. Since that job: (1) inbox item I010: shared.rs's reach, which both the identical-bytecode shortcut and the checker's ties rest on, now leaves the code open where a call into the JDK may come back into the application (an interface or overridable JDK method, an argument whose methods the JDK may call, a charset by name), and takes in the initializers of the application classes the code uses. bcrypt's loop methods call only array clone and IllegalArgumentException(String), so their ties stand: a capped probe takes over 208 summaries as before. (2) That refusal now says what the reference held at the loop's head and back at it, so a stop at the same place names the objects. Expected: verified. Otherwise the stop, with the objects named, is step 5's next finding (outcome.json search.native, the driver's last lines).
expected: prove.py ends 'verdict: verified (expected verified)' and exits 0; outcome.json has verdict verified and stated.vacuity.outside, and evidence.json is written
